disease_label_per_paper: Fatal fulminant hepatitis B in an HIV-positive man with high HBV DNA and escape/precore mutant viral populations
presentation_summary: 26-year-old Caucasian man was referred with jaundice, general fatigue, and anorexia; he denied known HBV/HIV exposure risks including intravenous drug use, surgery, tattoos, or piercing.

Admission labs showed platelet count 139 x 10^9/L, PT 34.4 seconds, total bilirubin 1.56 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 0.60 mg/dL, AST 2037 U/L, ALT 2317 U/L, LDH 1395 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase 180 U/L.
Abdominal sonography showed an enlarged liver with dishomogeneous structure and normal biliary tree.

He had an acute hepatitis B profile: HBsAg positive, HBeAg positive, weakly positive anti-HBc IgM and anti-HBc IgG, anti-HBe negative, negative acute HAV/HDV/CMV/EBV markers, negative HCV antibody/RNA, and high HBV DNA 1.5 x 10^9 copies/mL.
He was newly diagnosed with chronic HIV infection with CD4 count 12 cells/uL, CD8 count 323 cells/uL, CD4/CD8 ratio 0.04, and HIV RNA 3.6 x 10^5 copies/mL.
Over the following week, bilirubin rose to 12 mg/dL, ALT to 3378 U/L, AST to 4235 U/L, consciousness rapidly deteriorated, coagulation time became prolonged, and fulminant hepatitis B was diagnosed.
Lamivudine 200 mg/day was started on hospital day 12, but he died of liver failure three days later; before death HBV DNA remained high at 5 x 10^8 copies/mL.
